The R4SUB Evidence Schema

Source: vignettes/evidence-schema.Rmd
evidence-schema.Rmd

Every package in the R4SUB ecosystem reads and writes the same evidence table. A quality tool, a traceability engine, and a risk model all emit rows in this one shape, which is what lets r4subscore combine them into a single readiness score. This article is the formal specification of that table.

library(r4subcore)

The columns

evidence_schema_spec() returns the schema as a table: one row per column, its type, whether it is required, its controlled vocabulary if it has one, and a short description.

spec <- evidence_schema_spec()
knitr::kable(spec)
column type required allowed_values description
run_id character TRUE NA Identifier for the run that produced the evidence.
study_id character TRUE NA Study the evidence belongs to.
asset_type character TRUE dataset, define, program, validation, spec, other Kind of asset the check was run against.
asset_id character TRUE NA Identifier of the asset, for example a dataset name.
source_name character TRUE NA Tool or process that produced the evidence.
source_version character FALSE NA Version of the source tool or process.
indicator_id character TRUE NA Stable identifier for the check or indicator.
indicator_name character TRUE NA Human-readable name of the indicator.
indicator_domain character TRUE quality, trace, risk, usability Readiness pillar the indicator contributes to.
severity character TRUE info, low, medium, high, critical How serious a failure of this check is.
result character TRUE pass, fail, warn, na Outcome of the check.
metric_value double FALSE NA Numeric value behind the result, when there is one.
metric_unit character FALSE NA Unit for metric_value.
message character FALSE NA Free-text explanation of the result.
location character FALSE NA Where the finding sits, for example a variable or file.
evidence_payload character FALSE NA JSON payload with the raw detail behind the result.
created_at POSIXct TRUE NA Time the evidence row was created.

A row is one observation: a single check, run against a single asset, producing a single result. Required columns must be present and non-missing. Nullable columns may be NA.

Controlled vocabularies

Four columns are restricted to a fixed set of values. Using the canonical set keeps scoring and aggregation consistent across sources.

schema <- evidence_schema()
schema$asset_type$allowed
#> [1] "dataset"    "define"     "program"    "validation" "spec"      
#> [6] "other"
schema$indicator_domain$allowed
#> [1] "quality"   "trace"     "risk"      "usability"
schema$severity$allowed
#> [1] "info"     "low"      "medium"   "high"     "critical"
schema$result$allowed
#> [1] "pass" "fail" "warn" "na"

severity runs from info (no weight) to critical (full weight). indicator_domain names the readiness pillar the check feeds: quality, trace, risk, or usability. result is the outcome, where na means the check did not apply.

If your source uses different labels, canon_severity() and canon_result() map common aliases onto the canonical set:

canon_severity(c("HIGH", "warning", "Error"))
#> [1] "high"   "medium" "high"
canon_result(c("PASS", "Failed", "N/A"))
#> [1] "pass" "fail" "na"

Run context

run_id and study_id tie every row back to the run that produced it. Rather than set them by hand on each row, create a run context once and let as_evidence() fill them in:

ctx <- r4sub_run_context(study_id = "STUDY01", environment = "DEV")
#> ℹ Run context created: "R4S-20261025204223-wl4dieex"

ev <- as_evidence(
  data.frame(
    asset_type = "validation",
    asset_id = "ADSL",
    source_name = "pinnacle21",
    indicator_id = "SD0001",
    indicator_name = "Missing variable",
    indicator_domain = "quality",
    severity = "high",
    result = "fail",
    message = "Variable AGEU is missing",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  ctx = ctx
)
#> ✔ Evidence table created: 1 row

ev[, c("run_id", "study_id", "indicator_id", "severity", "result")]
#>                        run_id study_id indicator_id severity result
#> 1 R4S-20261025204223-wl4dieex  STUDY01       SD0001     high   fail

Validation

as_evidence() validates as it builds, and validate_evidence() checks an existing table against the specification: required columns present, types correct, and controlled vocabularies respected. A table that passes validate_evidence() is guaranteed to score.

validate_evidence(ev)

Because the specification is a function, downstream packages can rely on it directly rather than restating the column list. That is what keeps the ecosystem in step: there is one schema, and this is it.

Schema versioning

The schema will change over time: a new column, a widened vocabulary. So that a table written by one release can be recognized by another, every evidence table carries a schema version. as_evidence() stamps it, and evidence_schema_version() reports it.

evidence_schema_version()
#> [1] "1.0.0"
evidence_schema_version(ev)
#> [1] "1.0.0"

validate_evidence() reads the stamp. An unstamped table is tolerated, because a table can predate versioning or lose its stamp on a round-trip through CSV or JSON. A table stamped with a version this release does not recognize, including a version newer than the installed package, is refused rather than scored on guesswork. When a table is stamped with an older, known version, migrate_evidence() upgrades it to the current schema:

migrated <- migrate_evidence(ev)
evidence_schema_version(migrated)
#> [1] "1.0.0"

The policy is deliberately asymmetric: read older tables by migrating them forward, but never pretend to understand a newer one. That is what lets the ecosystem move without breaking tables already written.
